review: The hymn is Peter's confession turned to love: 1:1–8 is Matt 16:16 with Matt 27:29 and Ps 22:7, 2:1–8 is John 4:6–7 (the well) with John 11:35 (the grave) and Matt 9:36, and 3:1–8 is Phil 2:9–11 nearly verbatim with Rev 5:12.

2:5–8 name the Gospel scenes without narrating them: the well of John 4 and the grave of John 11 are the two places the hymn's love rests on, and the Hebrew keeps them as bare participial tableaux (וִישִׁיבָה … וּבְכִי), because the stanza is a list of what captivated the heart, not a gospel harmony.

1:4 בְּכִלְיוֹתַי וּבַצְּלָעוֹת — the Arabic وَالْحَنَايَا وَالضُّلُوع is 'the inmost parts and the ribs'; the Hebrew uses כִּלְיוֹתַי, the psalm's word for the inward parts (Ps 139:13), with צְלָעוֹת for the ribs, so the line says the love reached the body's frame and not only the feelings.

3:5–6 אֶכְרַע עַל־בִּרְכַּי / לֹא מִיִּרְאָה וָפַחַד — the Arabic سَوْفَ أَحْنِي رُكْبَتَيَّ لَيْسَ مِنْ خَوْفٍ وَرُعْب is deliberately the reverse of Phil 2:10's compelled bowing; the Hebrew keeps the same vocabulary and the negation, so the stanza's point (a voluntary knee) is audible against the quotation.
